public_rationale: The training-power component is supported: expanding frontier training requires more electrical power despite efficiency improvements. The exclusivity component is too strong on the ordinary reading. Research available before the post identified substantial algorithmic gains as well as a larger contribution from scaling. This finding does not establish that every increase in AI capability must increase a company's total electricity use.
limitations: The capability evidence uses historical language-model benchmarks and has uncertainty in separating algorithms from scale.
The electricity evidence concerns frontier training, not the complete operations of every big technology company.
Reading 'only potent trick' as merely 'the dominant method' would weaken the contradiction.

from_speaker: The only potent trick anyone seems to have is scaling

our_interpretation: In context, scaling means increasing the computing resources used to develop and operate frontier generative AI.
The ordinary reading contains two propositions: scaling is effectively the only substantial source of capability gains, and expanding AI computation increases electricity requirements.
I treat 'seems' as qualifying the exclusivity assertion, rather than deleting it.
The electricity assertion describes a directional causal relationship. It does not specify proportional growth or assert that efficiency can never improve.
The assessment concerns the technological relationship described in October 2024, not a forecast with a 2026 deadline.
criteria.support_condition: Research finds substantial capability gains attributable essentially only to scaling, and evidence connecting larger AI computing workloads to increased electricity requirements supports the energy component.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Substantial capability gains from algorithmic changes contradict the exclusivity component. Evidence that efficiency offsets expansion sufficiently to prevent electricity growth would challenge the energy component within the measured scope.
